title: 4. URINARY TRACK INJURIES DURING LAPROSCOPY AND THEIR PREVENTION.

blocks.content:
4. URINARY TRACK INJURIES DURING LAPROSCOPY AND THEIR PREVENTION.

•Most common major complication.
•91 times higher litigation with these injuries.

Urinary bladder:

•0.02 – 8.3%.
•Comonest site = midline above Inter/uretric bar.
•LAVH most common cause of bladder injury.

Damage can occur while:

•Suprapubic port.
•Separation of bladder from cervix

Prevention:

1.Knowledger of anatomy, technique and skill
2.Aoid suprapubic port insertion (higer failure => rupture in space of retizius surgical emphysema.
3.Bladdder deflation

Empty bladder not easily perforated.

4.Cystosubflation
-Dye stained Ringer lactate
-CO2
-Saline.

To identify margins of bladder in difficult surgeries but deflate before central & lateral seperation to avoid damage.

5.Adequate dissection of bladder from vaginal apex when cuff is sutured vaginaly and sepation done abdominally.
6.Safe electrosurgical usage.

Ureteric Injury:

•< 1% - 2%
•Subtotal hysterectomy = 0.6%
•Endometriosis = 21%.

Commonest site:

•Pelvic Brim
•Lateral to cervix
•Electrocautery 1/4th cases.
•12% pt have ureters < 0.5cm from cervix.

Ed BMI => ureters close to cervix.

Prevention:

•Knowledge of Anatomy
-Safe electrosurgery and meticulous technique.
-MRI or IVU help surgeon to check anatomy of ureters before surgery
•Magnified View
-To identify uretric peristallsis.
•Mobilization of ureters
-In complex cases upto 15cm (1/2 length) can be mobilized with out compromising blood supply.
•Ureteric stenting.
-Complex cases.

•Ureteroscopy
•Adequate reflection of bladder.

Types of Injury:

•Angulation
•Crush
•Ligation
•Thermal
•Laceration
•Transection
•Resection

Management:

⇨Crush
-Or minor needle injuries conservative if adequate peristalsis and perfusion is there
⇨Obstruction
-significant crush/ ligation.
-Stenting => 2 – 6 weeks.
⇨Lacerations
-Suturing + stenting.
⇨Angulation
-Stenting.
⇨Thermal
-Extensive + deep => excision + re-anastomosis + re-implantation.
⇨Transection

Upper 1/3 => ureterostomy/ end to end anastomosis with stenting.

Middle => uretro ureterostomy or trans uretro ureterostomy end to side anastomosis.

Trans => is not a 1st choice as it cuts the healthy ureter.

Lower => uretro neocyctostomy.

Tension free anastomosis is required, if not tension free due to short length of ureter, then go for Boari Flap or psoas hitch.

Psoas hitch:

•Bladder is mobilized and fixed with iliopsoas muscle tendon to fill the gape.

Boari flap:

•Upto 12 – 15 cm length can be added
•Transverse Incision, over bladdar
•Suturing in vertical line.

Retrograde urogram:

•To confirm uretric
•Patency @ end of healing period
